_comment: R22 (2026-08-06) — `--target-dev-hub` and its short form `-v` are now recognised targets. Before this, every packaging command was refused `no-explicit-target`: fail-closed for the right outcome by the wrong reason, which teaches a user the tool is broken rather than that the operation needs approval. Measured against Salesforce's own published examples, 430 of 763 refusals were no-explicit-target and `package version …` alone accounted for 20. THE WORRY WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: a staged note claimed that recognising the flag would unblock destructive Dev Hub operations. It does not, and the note was wrong. `package delete`, `package version delete` and `package uninstall` each carry a word in _DESTRUCTIVE_WORDS while no (topic, verb) rule claims them, so _destructive_shape already charges them `unrecognised-destructive` — measured identically before and after the change. What moved is the REASON, from 'you named no target' to 'this needs an operator-present token'. The allow cases below are the half that would have caught the change going the other way: they are what breaks if the flag is un-recognised, because a packaging WRITE would fall back to no-explicit-target.

fixtures.id: R22 deny: package version delete against a resolvable dev hub still needs a token
R22 deny: the short form -v resolves the same target and is gated the same
R22 deny: package uninstall removes an installed package and its data
R22 allow: creating a package version is ordinary packaging work, not destruction

tool_input.command: sf package version create --package MyPkg --target-dev-hub sf-cb-test

fixtures.id: R22 allow: listing package versions is a read and needs no authorization
R22 allow: package install is a write but not a destructive one
